deviations: endObjSeen is now part of the tail (EndObjTail.Seen, set wherever an endobj is found) rather than a separate flag copied beside it, as the refuter wrote. The copy of the tail carries it, so the design is the same with one field fewer. This replaced StreamEnds.HoldsEndObj in both the reader and the parser, and HoldsEndObj was removed; it saves a second endobj search of each read (see measurements).

The refuter's design covers only headers starting at a carried number. A header starting inside the 10-byte overlap, in the next read's own bytes, would still be wrong if each read were fed to the tail whole. So the search now feeds each read to the tail only up to the next read's start; copies are needed only for carried starts. Side effect: when a source stops giving bytes in the middle of one read, endObjSeen covers the bytes up to where the empty read started, not the 10 bytes of overlap after it. This can happen only on a source that shrinks during a single GetObject: a short-reading source converges a byte at a time to its end.
